abstract: Epigenetic dysregulation is a prominent feature in cancer as exemplified by frequent mutations in chromatin regulators, including the MLL/KMT2 family of histone methyltransferases. While MLL/KMT2A activity on H3K4 methylation is well documented, their non-canonical activities remain mostly unexplored. Here, we show that MLL1/KMT2A methylates Borealin K143 in the intrinsically disordered region essential for liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of chromosome passenger complex (CPC). Co-crystal structure highlights the distinct binding mode of the MLL1 SET domain with Borealin K143. Inhibiting MLL1 activity or mutating Borealin K143 to arginine perturbs CPC phase separation, reduces Aurora kinase B activity, and impairs resolution of erroneous kinetochore-microtubule attachments and sister chromatid cohesion. They significantly increase chromosome instability and aneuploidy in a subset of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), resulting in growth inhibition. These results demonstrate a non-redundant function of MLL1 in regulating inner centromere liquid condensates and genome stability via a non-canonical enzymatic activity.
